orders.description: Plaintiff's appeal from the order entered on or about May 8, 2018 granting summary judgment.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff alleged that he slipped on a slippery mold condition on a porch step at defendants' home while delivering a package. He testified that the step appeared safe and the porch was dry without dirt or debris; his experts asserted mold, moss and mildew.

legal_issues.finding: Defendants established that they did not create the alleged condition, and plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue.
Defendant's testimony of regular incident-free use and lack of awareness supported the absence of actual notice; opposition raised no triable issue.
Defendants established lack of constructive notice; plaintiff's own description did not show a visible and apparent condition, and later photographs did not establish one.

Mold/moss/mildew conclusions conflicted with plaintiff's testimony; slipperiness was speculative without touching the step or recreating the fall, and photographs taken over a year later were insufficient.

evidence_discussed.description: Defendant's use/awareness testimony and plaintiff's deposition describing a safe-looking, dry porch were considered.
Plaintiff's experts' condition and slipperiness opinions were rejected as speculative or conclusory.
Engineering expert's photographs taken more than a year after the accident did not establish an apparent slippery condition.

quality.notes: Private residential control is supported by defendants' home and their regular use of the steps; legal title is not inferred. Delivery activity is explicit but employment/contractor status is not, so injured_role is other. Mold/moss/mildew is an other hazard, not proven water or debris. Accident date is unstated. Expert insufficiency does not establish the absence of all possible hazards.

evidence.quote: Order, Supreme Court, New York County (Donald Miles, J.), entered on or about May 8, 2018, which granted defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, unanimously affirmed, without costs.

Defendants established their prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law in this action where plaintiff alleges that he slipped and fell on a slippery mold condition on a porch step at defendants' home when he was delivering a package.

Defendants demonstrated through the testimony of defendant Samuel Dimon that they did not create or have actual or constructive notice of the alleged dangerous condition, as they and their invitees regularly used the steps without incident and were not aware of any slippery mold condition

Defendants also relied on plaintiff's deposition testimony that before the accident, the porch step appeared safe, the porch area was dry, and there was no dirt or debris, which indicates that the alleged defective condition was not visible and apparent so as to constitute constructive notice
In opposition, plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact.

The conclusions of plaintiff's experts that there was mold, moss, and mildew on the steps were speculative and conclusory, as they were inconsistent with plaintiff's testimony regarding the condition of the steps
Moreover, the opinion of the experts that the moss was slippery is speculative, as they did not touch the step in question or attempt to recreate the circumstances surrounding plaintiff's fall

The photographs taken by the engineering expert over a year after the accident showing wood steps with a greenish tinge, does "not establish an apparent and visible slippery or otherwise dangerous condition on the stairs"

orders.description: Plaintiff's appeal, with leave granted, from the March 19, 2015 sua sponte dismissal order.
orders.trial_court_action: Dismissed the action pursuant to CPLR 3216 without reaching defendants' pending summary-judgment motion.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly slipped on leaves and candy wrappers while walking in defendants' parking lot.

legal_issues.finding: CPLR 3216 dismissal lacked the required specified neglect and advance notice/opportunity to be heard. Leave to appeal was granted, the order reversed, and the undecided negligence motion remitted for determination.

quality.notes: Procedural-only: no negligence merits resolved; the summary-judgment motion remains pending. Full reversal with consequential remittal is retained, not remand_only or mixed. Granting leave to appeal is not a second independently appealed order. Private lot control is attributed by the supplied text; associated retail use is not inferred from the defendant's name. Plaintiff's role, accident date and evidentiary materials concerning the fall are unstated.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is reversed, on the law, and the matter is remitted to the Supreme Court, Nassau County, for a determination of the defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint;
The plaintiff allegedly sustained personal injuries when she slipped and fell on leaves and candy wrappers while walking in the defendants' parking lot.

In an action, inter alia, to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals from an order of the Supreme Court, Nassau County (Feinman, J.), entered March 19, 2015, which, sua sponte, directed dismissal of the action pursuant to CPLR 3216.

Nonetheless, the court did not reach the merits of the defendants' motion and, instead, sua sponte, directed the dismissal of the action pursuant to CPLR 3216 based upon the plaintiff's failure to file the note of issue within 90 days of the certification order.
Here, the certification order did not set forth any specific conduct constituting neglect by the plaintiff.
Here, the Supreme Court failed to give the parties notice and an opportunity to be heard prior to considering whether to dismiss the action pursuant to CPLR 3216.
Since the statutory preconditions to dismissal were not met, the court erred in directing the dismissal of the action pursuant to CPLR 3216.
Although the parties raise arguments regarding the defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint, the Supreme Court did not decide that motion, and it remains pending and undecided
Accordingly, we remit the matter to the Supreme Court, Nassau County, for a determination of the defendants' motion for summary judgment.
Ordered that on the Court's own motion, the notice of appeal from the order is deemed to be an application for leave to appeal, and leave to appeal is granted

orders.description: Plaintiff's limited appeal from the August 9, 2016 order granting dismissal of the complaint.
orders.trial_court_action: Granted the branch of defendants' motion seeking summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

facts.factual_summary: While working on a mechanical system on a mall roof on July 31, 2013, plaintiff allegedly encountered a wooden stair that cracked beneath him. He jumped from the step to avoid falling.

legal_issues.finding: The court stated defendants' proof may have established noncreation, but did not rest the result on a definitive finding of noncreation.
The court stated the proof may have established lack of actual notice; constructive notice remained the dispositive deficiency.
Defendants supplied no evidence of the last pre-accident stair inspection and failed their initial lack-of-constructive-notice burden. Plaintiff's opposition need not be assessed.

quality.notes: The concrete incident account describes jumping to avoid a fall, not a slip/trip-and-fall. Generic legal language about when a plaintiff fell does not override that account. Substantive negligence review and full reversal of the appealed branch are preserved despite exclusion; the third-party-action caption does not make this third-party-only. Defendants' ownership/management are collective alternatives, not a finding that each held both roles. Work activity does not establish employee or contractor status. No specific inspection-record or testimony format is identified.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is reversed insofar as appealed from, on the law, with costs, and that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the complaint is denied.
On July 31, 2013, the plaintiff was working on a mechanical system on the roof of the Galleria Mall in White Plains, which was owned and/or managed by the defendants.
The plaintiff allegedly sustained personal injuries when, as he descended a small set of wooden stairs, one of the steps cracked while he was on it, and he jumped from the step to avoid falling.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the plaintiff appeals, as limited by his brief, from so much of an order of the Supreme Court, Westchester County (Jamieson, J.), entered August 9, 2016, as granted that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

Here, while the evidence submitted in support of the subject branch of the defendants' motion may have demonstrated, prima facie, that they did not create the alleged condition or have actual notice thereof, it failed to demonstrate, prima facie, that they did not have constructive notice of it.

Thus, in the absence of any evidence as to when they last inspected the staircase prior to the accident, they failed to establish, prima facie, that they lacked constructive notice of the allegedly defective condition of the step
In light of the defendants' failure to meet their prima facie burden on the subject branch of their motion, we need not consider the sufficiency of the plaintiff's opposition papers
Accordingly, the Supreme Court should have denied that branch of the defendants' motion which was for summary judgment dismissing the complaint.

orders.description: Defendants' limited appeal from the June 5, 2009 denial of summary judgment as to them.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied the appealing defendants' motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against them.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff allegedly tripped on an entry mat while entering a grocery store on October 18, 2005. He did not observe the mat before falling but described it as crumpled afterward; a defendant described seeing it flat 15 to 20 minutes earlier. SNS owned the property, and the parties also included a kiosk operator occupying rented store space.

legal_issues.finding: Appellants established noncreation and plaintiff raised no triable issue.
No prior accidents or complaints were known to the affiants; appellants established lack of actual notice and opposition raised no triable issue.
The specific account of flat mats 15 to 20 minutes before the fall established lack of constructive notice; plaintiff did not raise a triable issue.
Plaintiff's post-fall observation did not raise a triable issue whether the mat was crumpled before the fall; the court did not identify an alternate cause.
Unspecified remaining contentions were either newly raised on appeal or meritless; the opinion does not identify which fell in each category.

evidence_discussed.description: Plaintiff's deposition and Abdul Sattar's deposition/affidavit addressed the mat's condition and prior awareness.
Corporate principals' affidavits described no known prior accidents or complaints; Shazia Sattar also described her kiosk and lack of mat responsibility.

quality.notes: Full reversal of the entire appealed branch, not a mixed disposition; the four appellants do not create four independently appealed orders. Private ownership of the store property is explicit. Defendant roles are collective: owner, rented kiosk occupation and other store/corporate roles; no claim that each defendant held every role. Plaintiff is not expressly identified as a customer. Post-fall crumpling does not prove a pre-fall defect. Source OCR, including page marker and missing judgment wording, is preserved.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is reversed insofar as appealed from, on the law, with costs, and the motion of the defendants SNS Realty of Long Island, Inc., Abdul Sattar, RT Grocery, Inc., and Candi Pearsall, Inc., for summary dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against them is granted.
On October 18, 2005, at approximately 9:00 a.m., the plaintiff allegedly tripped and fell on an entry mat as he entered the Rite Time Dairy grocery store (hereinafter the store) in Cedarhurst.
The defendant SNS Realty of Long Island, Inc. (hereinafter SNS), was the owner of the property where the store was located.

In an action to recover damages for personal injuries, the defendants SNS Realty of Long Island, Inc., Abdul Sattar, RT Grocery, Inc., and Candi Pearsall, Inc., appeal, as limited by their brief, from so much of an order of the Supreme Court, Kings County (Schneier, J.), dated June 5, 2009, as denied their motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against them.
The plaintiff testified at his deposition that while he did not observe the condition of the mat prior to his fall, he noticed after he fell that it was “crumpled up like an accordion.”

Here, the defendants SNS, Abdul Sattar, RT Grocery, and Candi Pearsall, Inc. (hereinafter collectively the appellants), met their burden of establishing their prima facie entitlement to judgment as a matter of law by demonstrating that they neither created nor had actual or constructive notice of the allegedly dangerous floor mat.

Both Sattar, in his deposition and supporting affidavit, and Ratilal Patel, the president of RT Grocery, in a supporting affidavit, stated that they had no knowledge of anyone previously tripping or falling on the mats, and that no one had ever made a complaint to them about the mats

The appellants also submitted the affidavit of Shazia Sattar, the principal of the defendant Candi Pearsall, Inc., who maintained a kiosk within the store in space which she rented from RT Grocery. She had no ownership interest in RT Grocery, was not present in the store at the time of the plaintiff’s fall, and was not responsible for the floor mats.
In her affidavit, she stated that she had no knowledge of any prior trip-and-fall accidents in the store and that no one ever complained to her about the mats.

Moreover, the appellants met their prima facie burden on the issue of lack of constructive notice by submitting *1036 the deposition testimony and affidavit of Abdul Sattar that he had walked through the same entrance approximately 15 to 20 minutes prior to the plaintiffs fall and observed the mats to be flat on the floor
In opposition to the appellants’ prima facie showing, the plaintiff failed to raise a triable issue of fact as to whether the mat was crumpled before he fell
or whether the appellants created or had actual or constructive notice of the allegedly dangerous condition
Accordingly, the appellants’ motion for summary judgment dismissing the complaint insofar as asserted against them should have been granted.
The plaintiffs remaining contentions are either improperly raised for the first time on appeal or without merit.

orders.description: Defendant landlords' appeal from the April 27, 2009 order denying their summary-judgment motion.
orders.trial_court_action: Denied defendants' motion for summary judgment after finding triable questions of fact.

facts.factual_summary: Plaintiff slipped on ice in a driveway outside his apartment; the exact site and boundary between his landlords' and neighboring owners' property were disputed. He testified that a snowbank blocked the sidewalk and forced him onto the driveway. The parties differed over storm conditions and whether the driveway had been salted before the accident.

legal_issues.finding: Triable issues concerned ownership of the fall site and assumed maintenance responsibility through shoveling/salting. Failure to maintain defendants' admittedly owned sidewalk could also support negligence by forcing use of the driveway.
The court identified disputed notice and remediation timing without separately resolving actual knowledge; Cayea was there to salt, but the timing of actual salting was disputed.
Conflicting weather/testimony also left notice and time to respond unresolved; the court did not conclusively find constructive notice.
Testimony and meteorological data conflicted as to whether a storm was ongoing and whether a reasonable post-storm response time had elapsed.

evidence_discussed.description: Plaintiff and Cayea gave differing accounts of the accident site, weather and salting; both described snow removal from the sidewalk/driveway.
Neighboring owner testified about driveway ownership; the precise property boundary remained disputed.
Meteorological data were considered alongside conflicting testimony about an ongoing storm and notice.

quality.notes: The dispute is which private residential owner owned/controlled the fall site, not an unresolved public/private boundary: testimony attributes the driveway to neighboring owners and the side-of-house sidewalk is admittedly defendants' property. Ownership basis does not assert defendants owned the exact fall point. Driveway is location other, not an invented parking lot or public road. Only this landlords' order is independently appealed; the discontinued neighboring-owner action is history. Generic notice analysis is preserved without claiming a separate conclusive actual/constructive-notice determination. Accident date is unstated.

evidence.quote: Ordered that the order is affirmed, with costs.

Plaintiff slipped and fell on ice in the driveway outside his apartment, injuring his arm. He commenced this action against defendants, his landlords, alleging that they negligently maintained the property.
Appeal from an order of the Supreme Court (Demarest, J.), entered April 27, 2009 in St. Lawrence County, which, among other things, denied defendants’ motion for summary judgment.

Plaintiff testified that he fell near the edge of the driveway where it meets the sidewalk that runs along the side of the house where he lived. Defendant William Cayea testified that he found plaintiff 12 to 15 feet from where the driveway meets the sidewalk. Cayea and an owner of the neighboring property testified that the neighbors owned the driveway.
Questions of fact concerning whether defendants owned the property where plaintiff fell, and were thus responsible for maintaining it, precluded Supreme Court from granting summary judgment
Plaintiff testified that a snowbank prevented him from using the sidewalk and he was required to walk in the icy driveway to leave the property to attend a medical appointment on the day of his fall.
This failure to maintain the sidewalk—premises that are admittedly owned by defendants—could result in a finding of negligence

Cayea and plaintiff each testified that Cayea shoveled snow from and salted the sidewalk and driveway, raising questions concerning whether defendants exercised control over the driveway and thereby assumed a duty to maintain the driveway as a means of passage for plaintiff, who was their tenant

The parties’ testimony and meteorological data present conflicting versions of whether a storm was in progress so as to suspend defendants’ duty to remedy the dangerous condition until a reasonable time after the storm had ceased
That same conflicting evidence applies to whether defendants had notice of the icy condition and a sufficient time to deal with that condition
While Cayea was at the location to spread salt at around the time of plaintiff’s accident, the testimony diverged as to whether he had actually salted any part of the driveway prior to the accident
A triable issue exists as to whether Cayea’s actions met defendants’ obligation to remedy the dangerous condition within a reasonable time after it arose or they reasonably had notice of it.
Accordingly, Supreme Court properly denied defendants’ motion for summary judgment.
Plaintiff also commenced suit against the owners of the neighboring property. Supreme Court granted their motion for summary judgment and the parties have discontinued that action.
